papers.title: The Neurochemical Basis of High-Altitude Sleep Disruption: Disentangling Respiratory and Sleep-Circuit Mechanisms Toward Targeted Pharmacotherapy.
papers.abstract: High-altitude sleep disruption is a complex syndrome that many lowlanders experience when they reach plateaus above 2,500 meters, characterized by frequent awakenings, reduced slow-wave sleep, nocturnal hypoxemia, and central sleep apnea related to unstable ventilation. A prevailing assumption in high-altitude sleep medicine holds that stabilising ventilation, chiefly via acetazolamide, is sufficient to restore sleep quality. This assumption is challenged by a randomised controlled trial demonstrating that acetazolamide significantly reduced the apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) and improved oxygenation at 3,100 m while failing to restore N3 slow-wave sleep fraction, total sleep time, or sleep efficiency, parameters that remained impaired in both drug and placebo groups. This dissociation between respiratory and sleep-architectural outcomes constitutes the central scientific premise of the present review. An integrative neurochemical framework identifies four distinct sleep-circuit nodes disrupted by hypobaric hypoxia: impaired serotonergic synthesis, an adenosinergic paradox, orexin/hypocretin arousal instability, and locus coeruleus norepinephrine hyperactivation. Each node is mechanistically distinguishable yet interconnected with respiratory loop gain dynamics through shared neurotransmitter pathways, such as serotonin. Additionally, hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) is examined as a molecular bridge linking hypoxic signalling to circadian clock suppression and dysrhythmia of neurotransmitter synthesis. Current pharmacological agents are reappraised within this dual-target framework, and emerging therapeutic candidates, including GABA-A α₁-selective agents (Z-drugs), α₂-adrenoceptor agonists, orexin receptor antagonists, and adenosine A1-selective antagonists, are critically evaluated. A paradigm shift is proposed: effective management of high-altitude sleep disruption requires simultaneous targeting of both ventilatory control and sleep-circuit neurochemistry.

papers.title: Phytochemical Composition, Pharmacological Activities, and Clinical Evidence of Bacopa monnieri in Cognitive and Memory Enhancement.
papers.abstract: Bacopa monnieri (B. monnieri), a traditional Ayurvedic nootropic herb, has garnered growing scientific attention for its diverse pharmacological activities and potential therapeutic relevance across neurological, metabolic, inflammatory, and oncological disorders. This review consolidates current evidence on the phytochemical composition, bioactivity, molecular mechanisms, and clinical efficacy of B. monnieri and its major bioactive constituents, particularly bacosides, bacopasides, and bacopasaponins. Preclinical investigations have demonstrated that B. monnieri exhibits antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-amyloidogenic, and neuroprotective properties, mediated by modulation of cholinergic, serotonergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic systems and by enhancement of long-term potentiation, synaptic plasticity, and dendritic arborization. Emerging in silico and systems pharmacology approaches identify multi-target interactions and modulate pathways linked to neurodegeneration, glucose metabolism, and cancer progression. Clinical trials across healthy populations, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and Parkinson's disease indicate that chronic supplementation improves memory consolidation, cognitive processing, emotional well-being, and sleep architecture. Additionally, accumulating evidence supports its role in metabolic regulation, including enhanced insulin sensitivity, β-cell protection, and attenuation of diabetes-associated neurodegeneration, supported by multi-omics and network pharmacology analyses. Anticancer studies reveal synergistic effects of bacopaside derivatives in reducing tumour cell proliferation, migration, and aquaporin-mediated invasion. Collectively, the evidence positions B. monnieri as a multi-target botanical with translational promise in cognitive enhancement and as a complementary therapeutic candidate across metabolic, neurodegenerative, inflammatory, and cancer models. Future research should prioritize the development of standardized extracts, long-term safety evaluation, mechanistic validation in humans, and precision medicine stratification to optimize clinical applications.

papers.title: Rev-erb-α in Skeletal Muscle Adaptation: Integrating Circadian Control Mechanisms and Exercise Dynamic Responses.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms orchestrate a host of biological processes in a time-dependent manner to maintain homeostasis in response to exercise. Within this framework, Rev-erb-α, an intracellular nuclear receptor and transcriptional regulator, transcends its role in circadian rhythms to drive myogenesis, muscle remodeling, primary metabolism, and autophagy, underscoring its versatile, pleiotropic actions. This review consolidates experimental evidence from cell culture, genetically modified animal models, drug-based approaches and humans, highlighting the role of Rev-erb-α mechanisms in skeletal muscle and exercise adaptation. Recent frontier-of-knowledge data indicate that acute and chronic exercise elicit distinct Rev-erb-α signatures. There is bimodal regulation: Rev-erb-α is downregulated immediately post-exercise, followed by a subsequent increase, reflecting its primary role in pathway repression. In chronic conditions, the upregulation of Rev-erb-α can act as an adaptive mechanism that governs robust responses to energy demand and mitochondrial function, thereby coordinating the metabolic network, calcium homeostasis, and oxidative capacity. Also, Rev-erb-α overexpression or its pharmacological activation may reduce pathways associated with muscle atrophy, thereby preserving tissue function and muscle mass. Excitingly, higher physical activity levels increase the amplitude of Rev-erb-α over 24 h, enhancing health and performance. However, exercise timing determines the Rev-erb-α signature that affects downstream phenotypes in skeletal muscle. Thus, elucidating the mechanisms of regulation and action of the Rev-erb-α protein may offer new perspectives for improving or preserving muscle quality across different health conditions and diseases.

papers.title: Exploring the Neural Mechanisms of Acupuncture Stimulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Multimodal Neuroimaging Trial.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by restricted and repetitive behaviors and disturbances in social communication and interaction. Currently, there is no fundamental treatment for ASD, with only a few medications available for use on a limited basis to manage concomitant neuropsychiatric symptoms. The primary therapeutic goal of such treatments is to alleviate symptoms while maximizing the functional independence and quality of life of affected individuals. Many complementary and alternative medicine therapies have been reported to have effects on ASD symptoms; however, evidence is insufficient to confirm their clinical effectiveness. Acupuncture has traditionally been used as a complementary intervention to manage various neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases, including ASD, in East Asia. However, how acupuncture stimulation modulates neural activity at the macroscale level in individuals with ASD remains largely unknown. This study aims to elucidate disease-related brain alterations and explore the acute neural mechanisms underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD and in typically developing (TD) individuals, using a multimodal neuroimaging approach. This study was designed as a randomized, sham-controlled trial. In this stratified 2×2 design, 70 participants, including individuals with ASD (n=35) and TD controls (n=35), will each be randomly assigned to either the verum or sham acupuncture group, resulting in 4 groups. The verum acupuncture group will receive stimulation at specific acupoints clinically indicated for ASD, eliciting a deqi sensation. The sham acupuncture group will receive superficial needling at nonacupoints unrelated to ASD symptoms. Each group will undergo clinical assessments and multimodal neuroimaging measurements, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy and electroencephalography, before and after acupuncture stimulation. The primary outcome will be differences in resting state network metrics and relative band power in frontal areas by disease status. Secondary outcomes will include differences in these neural markers following acupuncture stimulation between the verum and sham groups, reflecting the group × intervention interaction. Exploratory outcomes will focus on identifying neural markers that correlate with clinical indicators of ASD. Recruitment began in April 2025. To date, 23 individuals with ASD and 21 TD individuals have participated in this study. The recruitment process is expected to continue until December 2026. ASD presents a significant socioeconomic burden, with no definitive treatment established to date. Although acupuncture is a widely applied intervention for various neurological conditions, including ASD, its large-scale neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. By using multimodal neuroimaging, the present study aims to investigate the immediate neural substrates underlying acupuncture stimulation in patients with ASD. These findings are expected to provide a robust neurobiological foundation for future longitudinal research and the development of evidence-based integrative strategies.

papers.title: Trends in Dispensing of Opioids and Benzodiazepines Among Older Adults Admitted for an Acute Hip Fracture Between 2008 and 2024 in Ontario, Canada.
papers.abstract: Opioids and benzodiazepines (BZDs) are commonly prescribed for managing pain, anxiety, and sleep-related problems following a hip fracture. Both opioids and BZDs carry risks of persistent dependence, falls, and mortality with long-term use. Despite these risks, Canada lacks standardized prescribing guidelines for older adults with hip fracture. We examined population-level trends in opioids and BZDs dispensing before hospitalization and up to 1-year post-discharge among older adults admitted for hip fractures in Ontario, Canada. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using linked health administrative data from ICES, Ontario, Canada. The cohort included individuals aged 66 years and older, residing in Ontario, admitted for an acute hip fracture between April 1, 2008, and March 31, 2024, and who survived for at least 275 days in the following year. Our primary outcome was post-discharge opioids and BZDs dispensed, defined as ≥ 1 prescription dispensed within 1-365 days following discharge. Secondary outcomes included pre-hospitalization dispensing, concurrent dispensing, and morphine equivalent dose. A total of 114,055 eligible older adults were admitted with hip fractures between 2008 and 2024. Overall, BZDs dispensing declined from 33.7% in 2008 to 13.3% in 2024, while opioids dispensing peaked in 2015 at 55.8% and decreased to 44.6% in 2024. Hydromorphone and combination drug therapy were the most frequently dispensed opioid drug classes during pre-hospitalization and post-discharge periods following a hip fracture. Concurrent opioids and BZDs dispensed following a hip fracture decreased from 3.7% in 2008 to 1% in 2024. Among individuals with 90 days of continuous opioid dispensed, most received < 50 mg average daily morphine equivalents. We observed a substantial reduction in BZDs dispensing. However, opioids dispensing remained consistently high. These findings underscore the need for future research on initiatives to reduce opioids use in post-fracture care, while recognizing that opioids remain an effective pain control drug.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

papers.title: Post-Exercise R-1,3-Butanediol did not Improve Markers of Fatigue or Recovery During a Multi-Stage Mountain Bike Race.
papers.abstract: Evidence suggests that exogenous ketosis (EK) induced by ketone monoester (KME) supports recovery and attenuates physiological stress during endurance exercise. However, the potential benefits of the ketone precursor R-1,3-butanediol (BDO) during real-world multi-stage cycling remain unknown. We investigated the effects of post-exercise BDO supplementation on physiological strain, dietary intake, hydration, cognitive function, sleep, and subjective recovery during the 2025 Absa Cape Epic mountain bike race. In this double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 18 trained mountain bikers (10 teams) completed an 8-day multi-stage race. Participants received either 87.5 mL ketone IQ (BDO) or a placebo (CON) twice daily (post-stage and pre-sleep). Heart rate, energy intake, sleep metrics, cognitive performance, and subjective stress-recovery were monitored throughout the race. BDO induced mild post-stage ketosis (∼1.0 mM β-hydroxybutyrate) from stage 1 onwards. Across the race, both groups demonstrated lower exercise heart rate, increased resting heart rate, increased energy and carbohydrate intake, and slower reaction time by stage 6, indicating accumulating physiological strain. BDO did not alter any of these effects compared with placebo. These findings suggest that the modest ketosis achieved with BDO was not effective under real-world racing conditions, highlighting the importance of formulation-specific and ecologically valid evaluations of exogenous ketosis strategies in future studies.

papers.title: Cell Village Captures Populational Heterogeneity of Sunitinib Cardiotoxicity.
papers.abstract: TKIs (tyrosine kinase inhibitors) have transformed cancer therapy; however, cardiotoxicity remains a frequent adverse effect with variable susceptibility among patients. For sunitinib, a commonly prescribed TKI, the molecular programs and functional features underlying this variability are not well defined, and clinically actionable predictors of cardiotoxicity risk remain lacking. To investigate interindividual variability in sunitinib-induced cardiotoxic responses, we implemented the Cell Village platform consisting of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes from 20 healthy donors. Pooled iPSCs were differentiated into cardiomyocytes, treated with sunitinib for 72 hours, followed by harvesting for single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Donor identity was determined using single nucleotide polymorphism-based demultiplexing. Additionally, individual line-specific transcriptomic responses to sunitinib were integrated with quantitative functional phenotyping (including contractility, electrophysiology, and recovery efficacy following tocotrienol treatment) in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes differentiated from a subset of 10 lines. Sunitinib induced a robust global transcriptional response characterized by dysregulation of tyrosine kinase signaling, cytoskeletal organization, ion channels, and calcium-handling pathways. Although the pathway-level changes were shared, individual donor lines displayed heterogeneity in both gene expression patterns and functional impairment. Across functional parameters, relaxation velocity was the most consistently correlated with toxicity severity. Integration of each iPSC line's functional data with the corresponding transcriptomic signatures identified gene modules related to calcium handling and structural organization strongly correlated with donor-specific toxicity and recovery indices. Pharmacological validation using tocotrienol demonstrated partial, donor-dependent improvement of sunitinib-related iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte impairments. This proof-of-concept study establishes a scalable, donor-resolved platform that links pooled transcriptomic profiling with functional toxicity and recovery phenotypes in human cardiomyocytes. By linking molecular perturbations to functional outcomes across genetically diverse backgrounds, this approach provides a framework for dissecting interindividual variability in TKI-associated cardiotoxicity. More broadly, it provides a foundation for extending population-scale cardiotoxicity assessment to additional drugs and protective interventions.

papers.title: Evolved differences in microglial cell biology between surface and cave populations of Astyanax mexicanus.
papers.abstract: Microglia govern multiple aspects of brain architecture and function by eliminating dying neurons and glia, stimulating neurogenesis, refining neural connections, and orchestrating immune responses. The Mexican tetra, Astyanax mexicanus, is a powerful model system for investigating the evolution of brain function, yet microglia have not been investigated in this system. A. mexicanus exists as surface- and cave-dwelling morphotypes with prominent behavioral and physiological differences. Notably, these evolved behavioral and physiological changes in the cave morphotype, including diminished immune responses and alterations in sleep, circadian rhythms, and sensory processing, are directly linked to known microglial functions in other systems, suggesting that evolved differences in microglia may shape brain circuitry adaptations in cavefish. Here we develop an experimental toolbox to examine microglial specification, dynamics, and function in A. mexicanus and perform comparative analysis of microglial cell biology between the surface and cave morphotypes. We find that the cave populations show increased numbers of microglia over developmental time relative to their surface counterparts. Microglia in A. mexicanus exhibit a rapid expansion in response to inflammatory cues, distinct from the inflammatory response observed in the related teleost zebrafish. Furthermore, microglia in cave populations exhibit lower lysosomal pH and expanded proteolytic compartments relative to surface morphotypes. Together, our observations reveal evolved differences in microglial cell biology between surface and cave populations of A. mexicanus and provide a framework to uncover novel neuroimmune mechanisms underlying the remarkable adaptations of the Mexican tetra.

papers.title: Prevalence of adult attention-deficit/ hyperactivity disorder symptoms among university students and their relation to sleeping duration, time management skills, and academic performance.
papers.abstract: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental condition that often persists from childhood into adulthood and is characterized by symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. In university students, these symptoms may negatively affect time management and academic performance. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of adult ADHD symptoms among university students at Jazan University, Saudi Arabia, and to examine their associations with time management skills and academic performance. We conducted a cross-sectional study at Jazan University, Jazan, Saudi Arabia. We used a multistage sampling technique. We distributed 763 online questionnaires to the university students; the response rate was 87% (664 questionnaires). Of them, 612 (80.2%) questionnaires were complete and included in the analysis. We recruited male and female students from the Colleges of Medicine, Nursing, Business Administration, and Engineering. Data were collected using validated self-administered questionnaires assessing ADHD symptoms, time management skills, and academic performance. Our study was conducted among Jazan University students, with a mean age of 21 years (SD = 1.6), and a predominance of male participants (64%). The prevalence of adult ADHD symptoms was 26% among Jazan University students. Significant associations were observed with female sex (odds ratio (OR) = 1.58), sleeping fewer than 4 hours per night (compared with ≥ 8 hours; OR = 2.46), and lower grade point average (GPA) (odds ratio (OR) = 2.10). Associations with the Academic Performance Scale (APS) and time management skills were inconsistent. Adult ADHD symptoms were more prevalent among Saudi university students than estimates reported in the global literature and were associated with female sex, insufficient sleep, and lower GPA. The inconsistent associations with academic performance measures and time management skills highlight the complexity of ADHD-related functional outcomes. These findings underscore the need for targeted interventions to support students' mental well-being and academic success.

papers.title: Longer sleep duration and the incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Sleep duration has been linked to adverse health outcomes, but its association with diabetic nephropathy remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the association between sleep duration and a composite endpoint of incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy. The study participants were 678 Japanese outpatients with type 2 diabetes. Lifestyle habits were assessed at baseline and at years 2 and/or 5. Mean values of lifestyle factors were calculated by averaging measurements from baseline to the date of endpoint onset or the end of follow-up. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used. During a follow-up of 6.0 ± 2.7 years, 215 participants experienced the endpoint. Among lifestyle factors, mean sleep duration was the only factor associated with the endpoint. Compared with participants sleeping <6 hours, the multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for mean sleep duration of 6 to <7, 7 to <8, and ≥8 hours were 1.08 (95% CI, 0.74-1.57), 1.56 (95% CI, 1.05-2.31), and 1.92 (95% CI, 1.15-3.19), respectively (P for trend = .003). This association remained significant after adjustment for key lifestyle and diabetes-related factors. The association was stronger in older participants and those with microalbuminuria or reduced kidney function. Longer, but not shorter, sleep duration is associated with an increased risk of incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy.

papers.title: Effect of Computer Screen Background Hues on Attention, Memory, and Visual Task Performance in Medical Students: A Repeated Measures Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Digital screen characteristics may influence visual comfort, circadian physiology, and cognitive performance. Although blue-enriched light has been extensively studied, less is known about whether the background hue of a computer screen affects short-duration cognitive task performance. This study compared balanced white, red-predominant, and blue-predominant computer-screen conditions with printed white paper in medical students. Thirty medical students completed four testing sessions one week apart in a repeated-measures design. The visual conditions were balanced white, red-predominant, and blue-predominant computer-screen hues, and printed white paper. Cognitive performance was assessed using an author-developed PQBD letter-identification task, a picture-difference task, comprehension-based multiple-choice questions (MCQs), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Differences across conditions were analyzed using the Friedman test, with Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc comparisons and Holm correction. Kendall's W was reported as an effect-size measure. Paper was associated with the highest performance on several tasks, while the red screen condition performed better than the balanced white screen on selected attention and recall outcomes. PQBD performance differed significantly across conditions (Friedman χ²(3) = 37.08, p < 0.001; Kendall's W = 0.412). Mean correct-response percentages were 71.40 ± 17.31% for white screen, 81.26 ± 10.35% for red screen, 80.63 ± 9.51% for blue screen, and 89.92 ± 11.54% for paper. Picture-difference performance also differed significantly (χ²(3) = 26.15, p < 0.001; W = 0.291), as did comprehension-based MCQ performance (χ²(3) = 52.03, p < 0.001; W = 0.578). Short-duration cognitive task performance differed across visual conditions in this exploratory repeated-measures study. Printed paper showed the highest performance on several tasks, while red-predominant screen hue was associated with better performance than balanced white on selected outcomes. Because the study used a small sample, fixed condition order, exploratory cognitive measures, and software-based rather than spectroradiometrically calibrated display settings, the findings should be interpreted cautiously. It appears that background hues of computer screens can affect task performance involving memory and concentration capabilities of medical students. Paper should be preferred in tasks requiring cognitive function, including memory and attention.

papers.title: Multicomponent non-pharmacological interventions for preventing delirium in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: It is necessary to evaluate the efficacy of multicomponent non-pharmacological interventions in preventing and managing intensive care unit (ICU) delirium and identify the most effective intervention combinations. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses A&I databases from inception to July 3, 2026, supplemented by a hand search of prior meta-analyses. Only randomized trials were included. Meta-analysis was performed using risk ratios (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals were used. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized controlled trials. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. The search identified 13 randomized controlled trials encompassing 5,525 patients. Multicomponent interventions significantly reduced delirium incidence (RR 0.53, 95% CI [0.36, 0.76], I2 = 72.5%, low-certainty evidence). The effect remained significant after excluding the two cluster-randomized trials (RR 0.45, 95% CI 0.30-0.67; I2 = 55.7%), the active-control trial (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.38-0.79; I2 = 73.0%), and all three trials simultaneously (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.31-0.70; I2 = 57.0%). In exploratory subgroup analysis, the within-subgroup pooled estimate for component pattern B, comprising cognitive assessment and stimulation, reorientation, sleep and environmental management, family or community support, and physical activity, showed a reduced incidence of delirium (RR 0.43, 95% CI [0.23, 0.82]); however, the formal test for subgroup differences was not significant (p = 0.604). No statistically significant effects were found for delirium duration, ICU or hospital length of stay, delirium-free days, or mortality. This study demonstrated that multi-component interventions effectively reduce delirium incidence in critically ill patients. The evidence did not establish that one component combination was superior to another. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024592821.

papers.title: Effects of Gallic Acid on Sleep and Circadian Rhythm in a Drosophila melanogaster Model of Fragile X Syndrome: An Integrative Behavioral and Bioinformatic Approach for Target Predictions.
papers.abstract: Sleep and circadian rhythm (CR) disturbances are hallmark features of fragile X syndrome (FXS), a rare genetic disorder caused by a full mutation of the FMR1 gene, resulting in reduced or absent FMR1 protein (FMRP). Despite the clear genetic etiology, targeted treatment for FXS remains unavailable. Natural polyphenol gallic acid (GA) has great potential to modulate neurobiological effects and is attracting increased pharmacological interest due to its low toxicity and capacity to modulate neuronal signaling. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the effects of GA on sleep and CR in the Drosophila melanogaster model of FXS and to further explore and propose potential gene and protein targets using a bioinformatic approach. GA effects on sleep and CR in seven different concentrations (100-1000 µM) were evaluated in dFmr1B55 mutants through high-resolution video monitoring. Bioinformatic analysis included protein-protein interaction and functional enrichment analysis linking the dFmr1 gene with GA. Behavioral results demonstrated that GA significantly modulates sleep and CR parameters in the fruit fly model of FXS in a concentration-dependent manner, with the most pronounced effect noticed at the lower tested concentration. Bioinformatic findings suggest that these effects may be mediated through the regulation of genes and proteins, including Rac1, bsk, Jra, Cyfip, and Dscam1, which are functionally connected to dFmr1 and implicated in sleep and CR processes. These results provide novel insights and preliminary findings into the potential of GA to ameliorate sleep and CR disturbances in the fruit fly model of FXS, offering a framework for future experimental validation.
papers.journal: The Yale journal of biology and medicine

papers.title: Case Report: Rapid resolution of psychogenic cough in an adolescent following bromazepam treatment.
papers.abstract: Somatic cough syndrome, formerly termed psychogenic cough or habit cough, is an under-recognized cause of chronic cough in pediatric populations, characterized by repetitive, dry, and honking cough that is absent during sleep. Behavioral interventions are first-line treatment with high success rates of 80%-90%. However, when access to behavioral therapy is unavailable, alternative pharmacological interventions, particularly benzodiazepines, have received minimal investigation in this population. I report a 13-year-old previously healthy male patient with abrupt-onset, near-continuous dry cough occurring every 2 seconds during waking hours. The cough had a distinctive honking quality and disappeared completely during sleep. The patient presented with severe impairment in function, including inability to eat for 3 days, multiple emergency presentations requiring intravenous hydration, and complete school absence. Medical evaluation, including physical examination, laboratory investigations, spirometry, and chest X-ray, was unremarkable. Empirical trials of inhaled bronchodilators and nasal corticosteroids yielded no improvement. Psychiatric assessment excluded psychotic features, depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and tic disorder but noted family stressors, including high expressed emotion and overprotective parenting behavior. Based on the sign of sleep-related cough cessation and exclusion of organic pathology, somatic cough syndrome was diagnosed. Given the severity of impairment and family circumstances precluding immediate behavioral therapy, bromazepam 3 mg orally was initiated. Within 24-36 hours, the cough resolved completely. At 3-month follow-up, the patient remained symptom-free without medication. He had returned to school and demonstrated normal eating patterns. This case demonstrates rapid and sustained resolution at 3-month follow-up of severe psychogenic cough following short-term bromazepam treatment in an adolescent. While behavioral therapy is still an evidence-based first-line treatment, this report suggests using benzodiazepines as a pharmacological intervention alternative when behavioral therapy is unavailable. The rapid response and sustained remission at 3-month follow-up are consistent with the hypothesis that benzodiazepines may interrupt the self-perpetuating cycle of anxiety and cough in somatic cough syndrome. Further research is needed for this case in pediatric populations to establish efficacy, safety, and optimal treatment duration.

papers.title: Multiomics Insights Linking Personal Care Products Exposure to Serum Lipid Profiles in Older Adults: The China BAPE Study.
papers.abstract: Personal care products (PCPs) are widespread environmental exposures, yet their combined and system-wide effects on serum lipid profiles in the aging population remain poorly understood. This study aimed to comprehensively assess the association between exposure to multiple PCPs and serum lipid profiles in healthy older adults and to explore underlying molecular pathways and biological mechanisms. We conducted a prospective panel study with five monthly follow-up surveys between September 2018 and January 2019 among 76 healthy older adults (60-69 years) in Jinan, China. This study measured urinary concentrations of PCPs, serum lipid markers, and multiomics profiles (transcriptomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics). We employed linear mixed-effects models to analyze exposure-outcome associations and integrated multiomics data with causal inference testing and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis to identify mediating biomolecules and biological mechanisms. Additional analyses examined the relationships of PCP exposures with inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress biomarkers, and electrocardiographic (ECG) parameters to provide functional support for the identified pathways and their associated phenotypic consequences. Four PCPs [Benzophenone-2 (BP-2), Benzophenone-3 (BP-3), 4-Hydroxy benzophenone (4-OHBP), and Ethyl p-Hydroxybenzoate (EtP)] were significantly associated with altered serum lipid profiles. Multiomics analyses suggested their convergence on a PPAR-centered immunometabolic network, with S100 signaling identified as a novel activation pathway. Specifically, BP-2 was associated with patterns consistent with IL-4/IL-13-mediated alternative macrophage activation, while PPAR appeared to be involved in inflammatory polarization and metabolic reprogramming. Cytokine analysis revealed associations between BP-2 and key inflammatory mediators (e.g., IL-1β), oxidative stress assessment linked BP-2 exposure to elevated markers of oxidative damage (e.g., 8-PGF2α), and ECG analysis associated BP-2 exposure with altered cardiac electrophysiology (e.g., QRS duration). These multifaceted findings suggest associations between PCP exposures and serum lipid profiles, and highlight the potential contribution to cardiovascular risk. Our findings provide integrated, multilayered evidence suggesting associations between exposure to PCPs and alterations in serum lipid profiles in older adults, bridging exposure profiles, biomolecular perturbations, and subclinical functional changes. These results serve as a hypothesis-generating theoretical foundation that, pending confirmation in larger studies or experimental validation, advances the understanding of environmental metabolic disruption in aging populations.

papers.title: Refractory Status Epilepticus Following Erroneous Intrathecal Injection of Tranexamic Acid: A Case Report and Long-Term Follow-Up and Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Accidental intrathecal injection of tranexamic acid (TXA) is a rare but catastrophic preventable adverse event associated with high mortality and severe neurological consequences. It represents a major neurological emergency that requires immediate specialized management. A 32-year-old man erroneously received an intrathecal injection of 300 mg of TXA instead of bupivacaine during a saphenous vein stripping procedure. He rapidly developed refractory myoclonic status epilepticus, sympathetic hyperactivity, and rhabdomyolysis. Management included multiple antiseizure medications, continuous EEG-guided sedation, and targeted use of neuromuscular blockade. The patient recovered without immediate neurological deficit but developed persistent cognitive impairment and posttraumatic stress disorder at follow-up. This case highlights the severe neurotoxicity of intrathecal TXA and the importance of early and aggressive intensive care management. It also underscores the need for long-term multidisciplinary follow-up for the assessment of anesthetic procedure-related complications.

papers.title: Is early-morning class exposure associated with lower positive mental health among university students? Conditional associations and heterogeneous profiles.
papers.abstract: University is a period of heightened vulnerability for student mental health, yet institutional schedules remain understudied as a modifiable determinant. Drawing on social zeitgeber theory, we tested whether early-morning class exposure is associated with positive mental health through social jetlag and emotion-regulation difficulties, whether bedtime procrastination conditions this association, and whether students' risk configurations are heterogeneous. Data were obtained from 1,437 university students in Sichuan and Yunnan, China. Early-morning class exposure was operationalized as the number of weekdays on which the first class began at or before 08:00. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, we tested direct, indirect, and moderated serial indirect associations while controlling for demographic covariates. Latent profile analysis then identified configurations of these variables, with positive mental health compared across profiles as a distal outcome. More frequent early-morning class exposure was associated with lower positive mental health (total effect β = -0.270, 95% CI [-0.316, -0.221]). This association operated partly through a serial indirect association: greater exposure predicted more social jetlag, which predicted more emotion-regulation difficulties. Emotion-regulation difficulties alone did not mediate the association independently. Bedtime procrastination amplified this process, strengthening the exposure-jetlag link at higher levels of procrastination (interaction β = 0.451, 95% CI [0.413, 0.489]). Latent profile analysis identified five distinct risk configurations: students combining frequent classes with stable sleep and effective emotion regulation reported the highest positive mental health, whereas those with co-occurring emotion-regulation difficulties and elevated schedule risk reported the lowest. These findings extend social zeitgeber theory to institutional course scheduling, showing that early-morning classes relate to students' positive mental health through a sequential temporal-psychological process that bedtime procrastination can intensify. Supporting student mental health may require attending jointly to institutional schedule design and individual sleep regulation, pending confirmation from longitudinal and objective-data designs.

papers.title: Beyond efficacy: the treatment lifecycle of incretin and multi-receptor agonists.
papers.abstract: Incretin and multi-receptor agonist therapies have delivered the widest range of cardiometabolic benefit of any pharmacological class in a generation, with documented benefit across obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and renal outcomes, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, obstructive sleep apnea, and metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. A substantial fraction of the cardiovascular benefit is weight independent. The pivotal trial evidence is now mature, extending to the dedicated tirzepatide cardiovascular outcome program. The clinical and system-level processes that govern long-term cardiovascular and metabolic benefit, however, lie largely outside the efficacy envelope that these trials measure. Real-world persistence is approximately one-third at 12 months in non-diabetic obesity. Discontinuation is dominated by cost rather than therapeutic failure. Weight and cardiometabolic gains revert toward baseline within months of abrupt cessation. Cyclical use has emerged as a common real-world pattern among adults who discontinue and then restart therapy. Our review proposes a lifecycle framework that organizes the evidence along the patient journey from initiation through titration, on-treatment trajectory, adverse-event landscape, persistence, discontinuation, and reinitiation. Tirzepatide serves as the analytical center of gravity; the selective GLP-1 receptor agonist literature serves as the mature comparator. Seven analytical positions are advanced, and five specific trial designs are named as the research agenda the field requires, four of which remain unaddressed. The work ahead is to align trials, prescribing pathways, and access systems with the chronic-pharmacotherapy reality of the class.

papers.title: Lifestyle factors or protective behaviors: which are more strongly associated with upper respiratory tract infections after COVID-19? A cross-sectional study of 1,535 Chinese college students.
papers.abstract: Respiratory pathogens have resurged following the COVID-19 pandemic. College students are socially active and often live or study in congregate settings, which may place them at continued risk of upper respiratory tract infection (URTI). To compare the strength of the associations of lifestyle factors and protective behaviors with the number of URTI episodes among college students in the post-COVID-19 period. We conducted a cross-sectional survey from June 1 to June 30, 2024, among 2,100 students at six universities in southeastern China. Students were eligible if their first SARS-CoV-2 infection had occurred at least 1 year before the survey. We collected the number of URTI episodes from June 1, 2023, to June 1, 2024, together with demographic, lifestyle, and protective-behavior data. The analysis included 1,535 valid questionnaires. Hierarchical negative binomial regression was used. Demographic variables were entered in the baseline model, after which lifestyle factors and protective behaviors were added sequentially. Their entry order was then reversed to compare the relative contribution of each variable group. When entered first into the baseline model, lifestyle factors produced a greater improvement in model fit than did protective behaviors (Δχ 2/df, 7.34 vs. 2.48; AIC, 4981.4 vs. 5067.9). Female sex, higher BMI categories, chronic diseases, COVID-19 vaccination ≥2 doses, daytime sleepiness (IRR, 1.768-2.324), sedentary, vigorous-intensity physical activity were associated with more URTI episodes, whereas sleep duration of at least 7 h and moderate-intensity physical activity were associated with fewer episodes (all p < 0.05). Among protective behaviors, only natural ventilation showed a consistent inverse association (IRR: 0.425-0.475; p < 0.05). Most other behaviors, including handwashing before meals, maintaining 1 m distance, avoiding touching the eyes/mouth/nose and public surfaces, and disinfecting phones and keys were not significantly associated with URTI episodes. Lifestyle factors were more strongly associated with URTI episodes than protective behaviors among college students in the post-COVID-19 period. These findings suggest that modifiable lifestyle factors, including sleep, physical activity, and sedentary behavior, as well as natural ventilation, may be relevant targets for campus health strategies.

papers.title: In Situ ATR-FTIR Analysis of Nalidixic Acid Degradation upon Oxygenation of Fe(II)-Sorbed Ferrihydrite and Maghemite Surfaces.
papers.abstract: The mechanisms of the abiotic degradation of antibiotics in redox-dynamic environments, such as aquifer sediments or hyporheic zones, remain poorly understood. This study investigates the transformation of nalidixic acid (NAL), a model quinolone antibiotic, triggered by the dark oxygenation of Fe-(II) sorbed onto two (oxyhydr)-oxides: nanomaghemite and ferrihydrite. Using in situ ATR-FTIR spectroscopy under continuous flow, we demonstrate that exposing the Fe-(II)-sorbed surfaces to dissolved O2 initiates the oxidation of adsorbed NAL over timescales of hours, without requiring light or added strong oxidants as H2O2. Real-time spectral analysis reveals mineral-dependent fates of transformation products. On Fe-(II)-sorbed maghemite, significant vibrational shifts indicate the oxidative cleavage of the pyridinic ring, mirroring mechanisms observed in heterogeneous Fenton systems, leading to the accumulation of adsorbed byproducts. Significant degradation of NAL is also observed upon oxygenation of Fe-(II)-sorbed ferrihydrite, with a slightly different end-product signal. These findings highlight that the aeration of Fe-(II)-bearing minerals is a potent natural pathway driving the deep structural transformation of recalcitrant contaminants during environmental redox cycles.

papers.title: Hyperactive Delirium Temporally Associated With Hydroxyzine in a Child With Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency Presenting With Psychotic Symptoms: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) metabolism caused by biallelic variants in ALDH5A1. The phenotype includes developmental delay, intellectual disability, seizures, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and other neurobehavioral symptoms. Psychotic symptoms are increasingly recognized in SSADHD but remain uncommon and incompletely characterized in children. In medically and neurodevelopmentally vulnerable patients, acute psychiatric decompensation may also be complicated by delirium, especially when severe sleep-wake disruption, poor intake, constipation, metabolic stress, and potentially deliriogenic medications are present. We describe a 12-year-old girl with intellectual disability, global developmental delay, abnormal prior neuroimaging, abnormal EEG findings, progressive weight loss, reduced oral intake, insomnia, and new-onset auditory and visual hallucinations. During hospitalization, she developed a fluctuating neurobehavioral syndrome marked by impaired attention, severe sleep-wake disruption, increased startle response, inconsolability, agitation, perceptual disturbances, and waxing and waning behavioral organization. These findings supported hyperactive delirium superimposed on psychotic symptoms rather than isolated psychosis. Hydroxyzine was ordered as 25 mg by mouth every 6 h as needed and was administered six times from hospital day 5 through early hospital day 7. The medication provided mixed short-term anxiolytic and sedating benefits but did not meaningfully reduce hallucinations or restore normal sleep. After hydroxyzine exposure, impaired attention, profound sleep-wake dysregulation, inconsolability, increased startle response, fluctuating agitation, and behavioral disorganization remained prominent, raising concern that hydroxyzine may have contributed to persistence or worsening of the acute confusional state in the setting of severe sleep deprivation, poor oral intake, constipation, neurologic vulnerability, and underlying SSADHD. Hydroxyzine was discontinued, and low-dose quetiapine was initiated together with environmental sleep-wake and reorientation interventions. Sleep, appetite, oral intake, and behavioral regulation subsequently improved. Diagnostic evaluation supported SSADHD, including elevated urinary 4-hydroxybutyric acid, characteristic MRI abnormalities of the globi pallidi and dentate nuclei, and a homozygous ALDH5A1 missense variant, NM_001080.3:c.434A >G (p.Glu145Gly), formally classified as a variant of uncertain significance but considered clinically concordant with the diagnosis. This case highlights SSADHD as an important consideration in children presenting with acute psychotic symptoms and altered mental status. It also underscores the importance of distinguishing psychotic symptoms from superimposed delirium in developmentally vulnerable patients. Because hallucinations, insomnia, poor intake, and behavioral dysregulation preceded hydroxyzine exposure and several competing contributors were present, hydroxyzine should be framed as a possible exacerbating or prolonging factor rather than the definitive sole cause of delirium. The case is therefore best described as hyperactive delirium temporally associated with, and possibly exacerbated by, hydroxyzine exposure.

papers.title: Alexander Disease Diagnosed in an Obstetrics Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
papers.abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare autosomal dominant leukodystrophy due to pathogenic variants in glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Adult-onset AxD type II presents with heterogeneous neurologic and neuropsychiatric symptoms. We report a unique case diagnosed in the postpartum period that mimicked posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). A 33-year-old gravida 2 para 1 at 36 weeks gestation presented with 10 days of progressive restlessness, delusions, insomnia, dysarthria, weight loss with inability to feed herself, and urinary/fecal incontinence. She underwent induction of labor due to concern for severe pre-eclampsia (elevated liver enzymes and creatine kinase, elevated blood pressure), received magnesium sulfate, and required emergent cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal status. However, her symptoms persisted postpartum. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed extensive bifrontal, periventricular, and pontine non-enhancing hyperintensities. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was normal including negative infectious, autoimmune, and paraneoplastic studies. Electroencephalography showed mild background slowing but no epileptiform activity. Empiric methylprednisolone and acyclovir had limited effects. Given the imaging findings, a leukodystrophy panel was ordered, which identified a heterozygous pathogenic GFAP variant (Arg79Leu), confirming a diagnosis of AxD type II. She improved with rehabilitation, with mild residual dysarthria at the 2-month follow-up. This is the first case report to describe an onset of AxD in the peripartum period. In peripartum patients with neurological symptoms whose course and MRI findings are atypical for PRES or other more common disorders, adult-onset neurogenetic disorders such as AxD should be considered. This diagnosis has important reproductive implications and warrants genetic counseling.

papers.title: Drug treatments for fibromyalgia: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials.
papers.abstract: To compare the effectiveness of drug treatments for the management of fibromyalgia. Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials. Medline, Embase, AMED (Allied and Complementary Medicine Database), PsycInfo, CINAHL, and Cochrane CENTRAL (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials), from inception to 13 January 2025. Parallel, crossover, and cluster randomised trials that enrolled adults (aged ≥18 years) with fibromyalgia, according to any published diagnostic criteria or as diagnosed by a physician. Trials compared commercially available, investigational, or discontinued drug treatments with another drug, the same drug at a different dose or regimen, placebo, or standard care. Treatments also included select vitamins and supplements, such as melatonin, vitamin D, vitamin B6, and omega 3 fatty acids. 151 eligible trials (32 592 participants) were included in this systematic review. Compared with placebo or usual care, low certainty evidence suggested that sodium oxybate, selective noradrenaline (norepinephrine) reuptake inhibitors (NRIs), serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), and gabapentinoids may increase the likelihood of patient reported meaningful improvement or recovery (risk difference 105 to 283 more per 1000 patients). Based on scores from the fibromyalgia impact questionnaire, low certainty evidence further suggested that sodium oxybate (mean difference -8.81, 95% confidence interval (CI) -11.78 to -5.84) and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) (mean difference -8.02, 95% CI -13.40 to -2.64) may reduce fibromyalgia symptoms, whereas tricyclic antidepressants, sodium oxybate, and gabapentinoids may improve sleep quality. No drug showed pooled effects on pain, physical health or mental health that met or exceeded a threshold for clinical importance. For sodium oxybate, selective NRIs, SNRIs, and cyclobenzaprine, responder analyses indicated that a potentially important proportion of patients achieved a reduction in pain of at least 30% (risk difference 111 to 202 more per 1000 patients). In addition, no drug increased the risk of discontinuing treatment or serious adverse events. This systematic review and network meta-analysis provides low certainty evidence that sodium oxybate, selective NRIs, SNRIs, gabapentinoids, tricyclic antidepressants, and SSRIs may provide typically small benefits in select outcomes for people with fibromyalgia. PROSPERO CRD42012003291.

papers.title: Subjective experience of listening to favorite songs and Murottal Al-Qur'an in young adult women: a quantitative EEG case series.
papers.abstract: Listening to music and Qur'anic murottal is a conscious auditory experience associated with beneficial health outcomes. Both activities share the same sensory modality called audition; however, murottal listening is additionally linked to spiritual belief, whereas music listening is not necessarily so, although both are reported to have favorable effects on health. The subjective, phenomenological aspect of conscious listening has rarely been examined alongside objective neurophysiological measurements. In this descriptive case series, four healthy 19-year-old female participants underwent a fixed-order recording session that compared mean alpha-band (8-12 Hz) power during listening (their favorite song and murottal, 3 min each), with mean alpha power during an eyes-closed, resting baseline, expressed as a relative percentage change: (E - B)/B × 100%. This index reflects relative alpha event-related desynchronization/synchronization (ERD/ERS) rather than the classical event-related potential. Heart rate and unstructured subjective reports were collected concurrently. Individual alpha ERD/ERS topography broadly aligned with participants' self-reported mental states-relaxation, visual imagery, and concentration-during both music and murottal listening, with notable between-subject variability in hemispheric lateralization. Given the small, non-randomized sample and the absence of inferential statistics, these observations are considered as hypothesis-generating rather than generalizable and are intended to inform the design of a larger, counterbalanced study.

papers.title: Gravity-awareness: a deep learning and LLM framework for predicting human adaptation to altered gravitational environments.
papers.abstract: Earth's gravity fundamentally shapes human behavior. The brain encodes this force as an internal model of gravity, enabling the prediction and interpretation of gravitational effects during perception and action. Understanding how this model adapts to altered gravity is critical for predicting human performance in spaceflight. We present a computational framework for modelling neurophysiological adaptation across diverse gravitational environments. The framework has two components trained on open-access data from altered-gravity studies, particularly parabolic flights. The first component (CorticalG) employs a lightweight multilayer perceptron neural network to predict gravity-dependent changes in EEG frequency bands, estimating cortical state under different gravitational loads. The second component (PhysioG) uses independent Gaussian process models to capture broader physiological responses, including heart rate variability, electrodermal activity, and motor control. To complement the quantitative modelling, we simulated subjective experience across gravitational environments using the Large Language Model (LLM) Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Physiological outputs prompted the model to generate narratives describing alertness, bodily awareness, and cognitive state across zero gravity, partial gravity of the Moon and Mars, and hypergravity. This framework provides a novel approach for investigating human adaptation to spaceflight. It offers a predictive tool to assess performance and resilience, supporting the design of future space exploration missions.

papers.title: PADA: perturbation-aware differential Riemannian attention for robust motor imagery decoding.
papers.abstract: Riemannian geometry models have significantly improved the robustness and performance of EEG-based motor imagery decoding and are better suited to small sample sizes; however, their ability to extract nonlinear and spatiotemporal variability features often falls short of Euclidean-based deep learning methods. To address these limitations, we introduce a perturbation-aware differential Riemannian attention mechanism (PADA). PADA develops a window-based learnable Riemannian module that maps informative segments onto the manifold to characterize nonlinear features while preserving local structure, together with a two-stream differential manifold attention mechanism. Tangent-space perturbations are used as a probe for feature instability, and attention weights that are hypersensitive to noise are differentially suppressed to distill robust geometric dependencies. On the BCI Competition IV-2a and Zhou2016 datasets, PADA achieved competitive clean-condition accuracies of 81.44% and 92.79%, respectively. Under 50% noise, its accuracy dropped by only 12%, achieving the best classification performance among the compared models. On a self-constructed dataset involving 227 subjects, PADA achieved up to 70.46% binary classification accuracy on the classic hand motor imagery task using only 12 training samples. These results indicate that PADA provides robust and effective feature learning for noisy and data-limited brain-computer interface applications.

papers.title: Sociodemographic correlates of perceived COVID-19 impact on movement behaviors in Croatian school-aged children.
papers.abstract: Levels of physical activity (PA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep, as important determinants of children's health and weight status, may have been significantly affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. This cross-sectional study aimed to determine factors associated with parental perception of COVID-19 negative impact in PA, SB, and sleep during the COVID-19 period, and whether the parental perception of COVID-19 negative impact was associated with actual post-lockdown behavioral levels among 2nd and 3rd grade elementary school students in Croatia. Data was gathered on a nationally representative sample of Croatian children participating in the CroCOSI 2021/2022 study. The final sample consisted of 5438 children (male = 51.4%, female = 48.6%) aged 7 to 10 years (M = 9.03, SD = 0.61). Risk and protective factors included children's weight status, demographics, and socioeconomic status (SES) variables. Parents completed the paper surveys on children's actual post-lockdown behavioral levels in PA, SB and sleep, and the perceived COVID-19 negative impact on these behaviors. Multinomial logistic regression models showed that the parental perception of negative COVID-19 impact on active play, screen time, and learning time was associated with various SES indicators, child-related variables, and degree of urbanization. Parents with high education levels were more likely to perceive a negative impact across all behaviors. Children of parents with high education compared to low had a higher likelihood of parental perception of COVID-19 negative impact on screen time (weekdays: OR = 0.48; CI = 0.40, 0.56; weekend: OR = 0.59; CI = 0.50, 0.70), learning time (OR = 0.49; CI = 0.41, 0.58), and active play (weekdays: OR = 0.57; CI = 0.48, 0.68; weekend: OR = 0.71; CI = 0.59, 0.86), but also to a higher likelihood of parents perceiving positive changes in active play. On the other hand, lower perceived family wealth increased the odds of parental perception of COVID-19 negative impact on active play (weekdays: OR = 1.40; CI = 1.08, 1.81; weekends: OR = 1.42; CI = 1.10, 1.82) and screen time (weekdays: OR = 1.36; CI = 1.07, 1.74; weekends: OR = 1.51; CI = 1.19, 1.91), while on weekends it was also linked to perceived positive changes in screen time (OR = 2.07; CI = 1.11, 3.83). Regarding the second study aim, complex samples of general linear models showed that the parental perception of negative COVID-19 impact was significantly associated with actual post-lockdown active play and screen time levels. A parental perception of COVID-19 negative impact on active play corresponded to about 12 min less active play per weekday and weekend day post-lockdown, while a parental perception of increased screen time was associated with about 12 min more screen time per weekday and 28 min more screen time per weekend day post-lockdown. The study results suggest that the parental perception of COVID-19 impact on children's movement behaviors varied according to sociodemographic factors of the children and their families, and was also associated with certain post-lockdown movement behavior in children. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health strategies that provide safe and accessible opportunities for play and physical activity while reducing excessive screen time. Continuous multisectoral efforts are important for promoting healthy lifestyles and preventing childhood obesity. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1186/s12982-026-02827-9.

papers.title: An evidence-weighted knowledge framework with path-aware reasoning for personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease.
papers.abstract: Healthy lifestyle management is essential for chronic disease prevention and long-term care. However, evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes is dispersed across diverse biomedical sources. This fragmentation makes it difficult for health professionals to efficiently retrieve and interpret evidence needed to inform personalized lifestyle guidance. We constructed an Evidence-Weighted Lifestyle Knowledge Graph (EW-LKG) to organize multidimensional lifestyle evidence by extracting structured triples from over 170,000 PubMed abstracts using schema-based large language model extraction with rule-guided verification. Each relation was assigned a heuristic confidence score based on study design hierarchy and aggregated supporting evidence to facilitate evidence-aware retrieval and reasoning. Path-aware retrieval and multi-hop reasoning were used to identify high-confidence evidence chains that support answer generation by large language models. Performance was evaluated by benchmark question answering across four large language models, external validation on the PubMedQA chronic disease subset, and expert scoring across 5 evaluation dimensions. We constructed an evidence-weighted, multidimensional lifestyle knowledge graph integrating diet, physical activity, sleep, stress-related, and social-behavioral factors, comprising 156 k entities and 202 k relations. Path-aware question answering improved accuracy across four large language models, with Qwen3-Max increased by 0.184, Llama-4-Maverick increased by 0.159, DeepSeek V3.2-Exp increased by 0.161 and GPT-5.2 increased by 0.159. Correct answers were also associated with higher PathScores (0.80 vs. 0.62), particularly for mechanism-mediated and multi-factor reasoning. Results showed insensitivity across alternative evidence weighting schemes, and source-disjoint validation on the lifestyle-domain benchmark suggested that gains derived from structured knowledge integration rather than corpus overlap; on the general-domain PQA-L split, gains were smaller and narrowed in the source-disjoint subset (0.598 vs. 0.528; 0.464 vs. 0.435). External validation on PubMedQA chronic disease questions yielded consistent performance. Expert evaluations across five dimensions showed an average gain of 4.34 points. The EW-LKG provides a structured approach for organizing literature-derived lifestyle evidence and selecting evidence-linked reasoning paths. In the evaluated datasets, path-aware retrieval improved QA accuracy across multiple LLMs. As an evidence-organizing framework, it may support more systematic and evidence-informed lifestyle management, while further validation in real-world clinical and public health settings is needed.

papers.title: Epidemiological study of dry eye disease in Gansu Province based on mathematical modeling: analysis of regional population characteristics and identification of risk factors.
papers.abstract: To investigate the epidemiological characteristics of dry eye disease (DED) in Gansu Province, examine the associations between regional population features and DED, and identify risk factors contributing to disease onset, thereby providing scientific evidence for clinical prevention, diagnosis, and intervention in this region. A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2024 to August 2025 using stratified, multi-stage cluster random sampling. A post hoc design-effect analysis was performed to quantify the influence of clustering on prevalence precision, and a mixed-effects logistic regression model was used as a sensitivity analysis to account for the hierarchical sampling structure. A total of 2,000 permanent residents aged 18 years or older were recruited from five geographic regions of Gansu Province. All participants completed a standardized questionnaire and ophthalmic examinations including tear film break-up time (TFBUT), corneal fluorescein staining (CFS), and the Schirmer I test (SIT). Factors associated with DED were evaluated using conventional multivariable logistic regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and random forest analysis. Climate type, elevation, sex, daily screen time, sleep quality, and smoking were associated with DED in the conventional multivariable model (all p < 0.05). The mixed-effects sensitivity analysis yielded generally, but not entirely, consistent findings after accounting for clustering. Based on mean decrease in accuracy, the random forest model ranked climate type as the most influential predictor, followed by daily screen time and sleep quality. The performance of the random forest model was favorable, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.832. The prevalence of DED in Gansu Province is affected by multiple factors related to regional environment, population characteristics, and lifestyle behaviors. Climate type, daily screen time and sleep quality are key risk factors. Public health interventions should prioritize high-risk regions and high-risk populations.

papers.title: Case Report: Primary aldosteronism coexisting with adrenal insufficiency in a 73-year-old woman with paradoxical hyponatremia.
papers.abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) and autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 2 (APS-2) represent opposing ends of adrenal pathology-hyperfunction versus hypofunction. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and diagnostically challenging. A 73-year-old woman with a 30-year history of refractory hypertension and recent hyponatremia was diagnosed with PA (aldosterone-to-renin ratio 29.11, positive captopril challenge, left adrenal hyperplasia). Spironolactone controlled blood pressure but paradoxically worsened hyponatremia. Two independent circadian cortisol profiles confirmed persistently low cortisol with preserved normal rhythm (first: 118.65/100.80/50.25 nmol/L; second: 133.34/71.62/39.12 nmol/L at 08:00/16:00/00:00). In contrast, plasma ACTH levels sent to an external laboratory showed no circadian variation (08:00 7.19 pmol/L, 16:00 1.21 pmol/L, 00:00 1.68 pmol/L; reference 1.60-13.90 pmol/L). This discordance-preserved cortisol rhythmicity with absent ACTH rhythm-raised the possibility of a preanalytical artifact rather than secondary adrenal insufficiency, although this inference could not be definitively proven. Physical examination revealed skin hyperpigmentation, and her history of Hashimoto's thyroiditis supported a clinically probable diagnosis of APS-2 (clinically probable Addison's disease with autoimmune thyroid disease), given the absence of confirmatory 21-hydroxylase antibody testing and ACTH-stimulation testing. Prednisone 5 mg daily was added to her regimen of spironolactone and levothyroxine. Her symptoms resolved, and serum sodium normalized. This report describes a rare case of primary aldosteronism occurring in the setting of clinically probable APS-2. The discordant cortisol-ACTH pattern serves as a critical reminder that ACTH is highly labile; clinicians must interpret results holistically, integrating clinical context and circadian patterns, and remain mindful of diagnostic uncertainty when confirmatory assays cannot be completed.

papers.title: Metabolic and neuropathic outcomes following combined sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy and adjunctive acupuncture in obese patients with diabetic neuropathy: a case series.
papers.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are associated with chronic metabolic dysregulation and microvascular complications, including diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN). This case series describes metabolic and patient reported outcomes during ongoing empagliflozin therapy with adjunctive acupuncture treatment. The prospective observational case series included three adult participants with obesity, T2DM, and symptom defined DPN. All participants received empagliflozin 10 mg daily for at least 4 weeks before enrollment and continued treatment while receiving standardized acupuncture twice weekly for 10 weeks. Primary outcomes included body weight, body mass index (BMI), and waist circumference. Secondary outcomes included neuropathic pain intensity assessed using the visual analogue scale (VAS), sleep quality measured by a single-item sleep quality score, and fatigue assessed using the fatigue severity scale were recorded at baseline and week 10. All participants completed the intervention without adverse events. The body weight decreased by 4-9 kg, BMI by 1.2-3.5 kg/m2, and waist circumference by 5-10 cm. VAS reduction range from 2 to 4 points, sleep quality and fatigue scores also improved consistently in all cases. Exploratory outcomes indicated enhanced mobility, reduced nocturnal neuropathic symptoms, and high treatment tolerability. Combined therapy with SGLT2 inhibitors and acupuncture was associated with improvements in metabolic, neuropathic, and functional outcomes in obese patients with T2DM, and DPN. These findings suggest that a potential multidimensional therapeutic approach, however, larger controlled studies are required to confirm efficacy.

papers.title: Earlier bedtime at 1.5 years is associated with greater height gain at 3 years of age: a nationwide birth cohort study of the Japan environment and children's study.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have shown inconsistent associations between sleep duration and height gain in early childhood. The relationships of bedtime and nighttime awakenings with growth remain unclear. We investigated whether sleep characteristics at 1.5 years were associated with subsequent height gain. Forty-nine thousand two hundred eight singleton, term toddlers classified as appropriate for gestational age were selected from the Japan Environment and Children's Study. Nighttime sleep was defined as sleep between 20:00 and 07:59. Nighttime sleep duration, bedtime, and nighttime awakenings were categorized as long (≥10 h) or short (<10 h), early (20:00-21:59) or late (≥22:00), and infrequent (<3) or frequent (≥3), respectively. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine associations with height and height standard deviation scores (SDS). The early bedtime group showed greater monthly increases in height and height SDS than the late bedtime group, corresponding to 18-month differences of 0.13 cm (B = 7.21 × 10-3 cm/month, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.06 to 0.20; p < 0.001) and 0.046 SD (B = 2.53 × 10-3 SD/month, 95% CI 0.027 to 0.064; p < 0.001), respectively. The long sleep group did not differ significantly from the short sleep group in either outcome in the primary multivariable model. In continuous analyses, sleep duration was significantly associated with height gain, but not with height SDS gain. In an additional analysis including sleep outside the predefined nighttime window, the >14-h group showed smaller increases in height and height SDS than the 11-14-h group, whereas the <11-h group did not differ significantly from the 11-14-h group. The infrequent nighttime awakenings group did not differ significantly from the frequent nighttime awakenings group in either outcome. Earlier bedtime at 1.5 years was associated with greater height gain, although the magnitude of the association was small. The associations of sleep duration with height gain varied between nighttime and 24-h sleep analyses. The observed association with earlier bedtime may have practical relevance because bedtime can be discussed during routine child health guidance; however, given the observational study design, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal effect.

papers.title: Night-shift work is associated with peripheral clock gene dysregulation and circadian transcriptional network remodeling in female healthcare workers.
papers.abstract: Night-shift work disrupts the circadian-melatonin axis through chronic light-at-night exposure and has been associated with metabolic, inflammatory, cardiovascular, and cancer-related disorders, but peripheral molecular signatures of occupational chronodisruption remain incompletely characterized. Female healthcare workers (HCWs), frequently exposed to prolonged night-shift schedules, represent a relevant study population. In a previous computational study, we identified a deregulated circadian gene panel (CLOCK, TEF, PER1, and PER3) suggestive of transcriptional remodeling in exposed workers. Here, we experimentally validated this signature and investigated the non-canonical circadian transcription factor YY1. Ninety-three female HCWs (47 day-shift, DSW; 46 night-shift workers, NSW) participated in the study. Peripheral blood expression of CLOCK, TEF, PER1, PER3, and YY1 was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations with shift-work status and exposure metrics were evaluated using multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, reproductive, lifestyle, and sleep-related covariates. Correlation, principal component, and clustering analyses were used to characterize transcriptional organization. Compared with DSW, NSW exhibited significantly lower expression of CLOCK (p = 0.0362), TEF (p < 0.0001), and PER1 (p = 0.0003), whereas PER3 expression was unchanged (p = 0.7978). TEF and CLOCK expression progressively declined with longer duration and higher cumulative night-shift exposure. TEF showed excellent in-sample discrimination between groups (AUC = 0.925), while a four-gene model achieved an AUC of 0.940. YY1 expression was reduced in NSW (p = 0.0019), decreased across long-duration and high-exposure categories, and further improved multigene classification performance (AUC = 0.976). Network analyses revealed disrupted coordination among CLOCK, TEF, and PER1, whereas PER3 maintained stable expression despite reduced integration within the transcriptional network. Night-shift work exposure is associated with coordinated downregulation of CLOCK, TEF, and PER1, altered transcriptional network organization, and reduced YY1 expression. While PER3 expression is preserved, its network connectivity is selectively weakened in exposed workers. These findings identify peripheral transcriptional signatures that may provide a basis for future biomarker development and exposure characterization and support further investigation of chronobiology-driven preventive strategies within a precision medicine framework.

papers.title: PKD2 structural destabilization drives primary cilia degeneration and ADPKD pathogenicity.
papers.abstract: Human variants in renal polycystins (PKD1, PKD2) are responsible for most forms of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), a common genetic disorder without curative drug treatment. Renal polycystins form ion channels in primary cilia, but our understanding of their molecular dysregulation caused by disease-associated variants is limited. Using cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), primary cilia electrophysiology and super-resolution analysis, we investigated the mechanistic impact and pathogenic potential of the disease-associated PKD2 missense variant (D511V) located within the channel's voltage sensor domain (VSD). Our findings define how this mutation neutralizes critical transmembrane charge interactions, which attenuates PKD2 protein stability resulting in abolished ciliary channel trafficking and function in membranes. To assess the pathogenic effect of this variant in vivo , we generated novel mouse strains carrying the analogous PKD2 mutation in combination with a conditional floxed allele ( Pkd2 D509V/fl ) that exhibit renal tubule primary cilia degeneration and develop rapid renal cysts. Our results establish a clear direct correlation between the in vitro molecular dysfunction and phenotypic in vivo consequences while providing a valuable tool to evaluate ADPKD therapeutic interventions. ADPKD is a genetic kidney disorder affecting millions of patients globally and is primarily caused by variants in renal polycystin genes (PKD1, PKD2). Polycystins function as ion channel subunits in primary cilia but the mechanistic impact and cystogenic propensity of disease-associated variants remain poorly defined. The authors employ advanced methodologies including cryo-EM to uncover distinct structurally destabilizing effects of a human PKD2 mutation, while generating a new mouse model which genetically expresses the same variant and recapitulates the human disease. The findings define primary cilia degeneration results from PKD2 hypostasis and establish new tools to assess ADPKD therapies.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and slow-wave sleep with plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Data on how sleep architecture relates to progression of plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers remains limited. Sixty-four cognitively unimpaired older adults (ages 55-90) underwent plasma collection twice 2.6 years apart and polysomnography proximate to the first plasma collection. Plasma amyloid beta (Aβ) 42 and 40 were measured via mass spectrometry. Frontal slow-wave activity (SWA) was inversely associated with plasma Aβ42/40 at cross-section in bivariate analysis and in a covariate-adjusted model. In comparison, low rapid eye movement (REM) sleep percentage was associated with a large longitudinal decline in annualized blood-based Aβ42/40. In exploratory analyses, the association between low REM sleep percentage and faster decline in Aβ42/40 ratio was stronger in the amyloid-positive group. In cognitively unimpaired older adults, non-REM SWA correlates with cross-sectional amyloid load, whereas REM sleep may predict accelerated amyloid accumulation in preclinical stage, suggesting both may serve as early biomarkers and modifiable interventional targets.
